title: Second largest
description:
Write `int secondLargest(const std::vector<int>& values)`.

It returns the largest value that is **strictly smaller** than the maximum. For `{ 4, 9, 7, 9 }` the answer is 7. If every element is the same (so there is no smaller value), return that value. The vector always has at least one element.

Do it in a single pass, keeping track of two things as you go: the largest so far and the runner-up.
hints: When you meet a new largest value, the old largest becomes the runner-up. When you meet a value that is below the largest but above the runner-up, it becomes the new runner-up.
